narrative.overview:
Hamna's working studio ledger sits open on a screen: a laid-paper folio in warm ivory-gold, ruled in fine browned-ink hairlines at a fixed 34px row pitch, with a maroon henna stamp as the voice and a single gold numeral where the artist's hand counts. The bride's wedding day is an entry inside the book — a dated appointment card threaded through the ruled page like a real booking, with the reserve action living in the card. Nothing is posterized; the surface reads as the artist's own record, opened to a day being drawn.

The palette is a five-strata ink world, not a color system: laid-paper field, browned ink for structure, maroon henna for voice, rust for a brief underline of action, gold for the hand. Type is one warm serif setting every word — no secondary face, no system UI face — with a thin italic reserved for annotations, marginal voices in the ledger's own hand. Borders are drawable one-pixel hairlines; depth is a ruled line, a whisper of the stain, and the book's own soft fall shadow. Density is comfortable and airy; the page breathes between the masthead rule, the service entries, and the close.
keyCharacteristics: Ledger: laid-paper pages, 2px browning-ink rules, 34px hairline row pitch, needle-hole gutter, tabular figures in dates and counters
Voice: maroon henna ink for the brand, gold numerals for the hand, rust underlines for the words that act
One serif voice: Fraunces for every word; thin italic only for annotations and the closing line
The card: an appointment is the one threaded surface in the ledger, carrying the primary action
The stain: one hand-drawn svg curl under the closing line; becomes the booking that fills the day

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Henna is the voice; gold is the hand. Henna owns words that brand or count; gold appears only as small numerals and labels. Neither is ever a fill across a large surface, and the two never compete on the same element.

rules.name: The Warm-Ink Rule
rules.body: No pure white, no pure black, no gray. The lightest surface is #FBF4E7 paper, the darkest is #4A2C16 ink brown, and every neutral is warmed by the ivory field it sits on.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Structure is drawn with 1px or 2px lines of sandline and ink brown. The page's one hard rule is the 2px ink-brown masthead line; below everything sits on hairlines, never thick borders.

rules.name: The One Serif Rule
rules.body: One serif family sets every word — Fraunces with Georgia fallback. No sans, no mono, no system UI face anywhere. A second face signals the poster; this system never leaves the ledger.

rules.name: The Thin Italic Rule
rules.body: Italic means annotation. Only the marginal notes, the masthead sub-line, and the closing hand-line are set italic, always thinned to 400 weight; nothing else on the page is allowed an italic.

rules.name: The Ruled-Page Rule
rules.body: Structure is drawn on the paper with ink lines, never embossed with shadow. Shadow belongs only to the sheet's own fall and to the one card lifted off it; an element that needs to feel present is drawn with a rule, not raised with a hard offset shadow.

rules.name: The Warm-Shadow Rule
rules.body: All shadows are tinted ink brown (rgba(74,44,22,…)), never pure black. A black shadow looks like a digital overlay; a warm shadow looks like paper resting on paper.

rules.name: The No-Corner Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are square, squared off at 2px at most. Rounded corners, pills, and chips read as generic product UI; a ledger sheet is never pillowed.

dos: Do set every word in Fraunces (Georgia fallback); the one serif voice is the system.
Do rule structure with 1px sandline hairlines and reserve the paper's hard 2px ink-brown line for ledger mastheads and the house rule.
Do let henna own the words that brand or count — the name, the notes, the button, the counters.
Do show gold as small numerals and labels only, never as fill.
Do keep the appointment card on ivory with its sandline border and warm lift — the one raised surface in the ledger.
Do let the reserve button's label speak at booking ("Drawing the day…" → "This slot is yours"); paper that answers is the hand at work.
Do keep 34px as the row pitch for the page's hairline rules so entries sit on ruled lines.
donts: Don't introduce a second typeface, a sans face, or a monospace — the ledger has one voice.
Don't use a pure white, pure black, or gray; every surface is warmed by the ivory field.
Don't set italic anywhere except annotations, the masthead sub-line, and the closing hand-line.
Don't use rounded corners, pills, or chips; surfaces are squared at 2px max and the page is square.
Don't raise hard offset shadows; depth is 2px ink rules, the page's fall, and the card's warm lift.
Don't move the needle-hole gutter or the colored stain beyond the ledger's own paper — the system lives inside the page.
Don't apply the wide-tracked uppercase ledger labels inside body prose; the uppercase voice is reserved for labels, folios, and counters.
